children: The search for the next HDFC Bank chief executive officer seems to have started, with chairman Rajiv Kumar said to be taking the lead in the selection process. A list of internal and external candidates has been drawn up by the chairman, in consultation with the nomination and remuneration committee (NRC) members of the board.

"Members of NRC, including the chairman, have started reaching out to a few bankers outside of HDFC Bank," said a person aware of the development. Kumar is also on the NRC, which is chaired by Harsh Kumar Banwala. The board, according to an August 29 media statement, is committed to appointing a successor to managing director and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, well before October 26,when his 30-year career is set to end at the bank.
According to sources, the hunt for the next CEO formally began on August 29, hours after Jagdishan told the board of his decision to not seek a third term.
email to HDFC Bank seeking confirmation on finding a successor to Jagdishan remained unanswered. Kumar could not be reached immediately for comments.

Among senior executives, Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director (DMD), is perceived to be the front-runner. Bharucha has been associated with the country’s largest private lender since 1995 and is a year senior to Jagdishan in terms of his tenure at the bank. However, given that he was first appointed to the board as executive director in 2014 and has been the bank's longest serving executive director, he has just about three years left to serve on the board, thanks to a regulatory ceiling capping tenure of executive bank directors at 15 years. "Bharucha may qualify only for a three-year stint as the bank's chief unless the RBI changes this rule," said a senior executive who didn't want to be named.
He also said there is depth of talent within the bank beyond Bharucha for the board to consider, though he refrained from revealing names.

However, another senior executive said that at this juncture it is not clear whether only an insider would be the board's natural choice. "The plain read of August 29 stock exchange release suggests that an internal candidate stands a high chance. However, given that feelers have already been given to some bankers, both from private and PSU banks and other financial services outfits, it's a 50:50 toss-up between internal and external names," he said.

"The chairman and a few members of NRC started engaging with bankers outside HDFC Bank for the MD & CEO role since the start of August," said the person cited above. He did not rule out the possibility of an interim MD & CEO being appointed for a shorter tenure while the committee examines "outsider" profiles.

Bankers, who according to sources are in the NRC's list of preferred candidates, are said to include State Bank of India's Ashwini Tewari, Tata Capital's Rajiv Sabharwal, ICICI Bank's Rakesh Jha, ICICI Life's Anup Bagchi and Aditya Birla Capital's Vishaka Mulye.

Moneycontrol has not independently confirmed with these executives their interest in the top position in HDFC Bank. News reports also suggest SBI's former chairman Dinesh Khara could also be a contender, though sources say he could also be roped in for a board position.

It is understood that some of the recent developments at the bank, which have pointed to the need for beefing up governance could be a compelling reason for the board to consider bankers outside HDFC. "HDFC Bank is highly process driven and it would not be challenging for an outsider to quickly adapt to the bank," said a senior executive who didn't want to be named.

title: HDFC chairman Rajiv Kumar to play a pivotal role in CEO selection, say sources
